simple.meaning: דּוּךְ (dûwk) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to bruise in a mortar.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Numbers, beginning at Numbers 11:8. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוּךְ (H1743) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: דּוּךְ (dûwk) / H1743 is traced through Numbers 11:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1743. duk [ דּוּךְ ] verb pound, beat (in mortar) (Late Hebrew & Aramaic id. , Arabic ; compare also Assyrian dâku , kill COT Gloss ). — Qal. Perfect 3plural בַּמְּדֹכָה דָּכ֨וּ ( milra` ) Num 11:8 (|| בָרֵחַיִם טָֽחֲנוּ ).

occurrences.englishText: The people went around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.
